title: Long words, syllable by syllable
goal: Type any word from its sound: one syllable per stroke, split at each break, join key on every stroke after the first.

items: Say it slowly; split where you hear a break.
Strike each syllable like a one-syllable word (lesson 7).
Hold the join key on every stroke after the first.

blocks.x: Without `+`, each stroke is a separate word (*column*, *prah*, *meyez*).

items: **A weak last syllable drops its vowel**, like an ending: [[table|TAEU/+-BL]], [[lemon|HRE/+PH-PB]].

**A weak vowel you do strike is `U`** (a weak short i is `EU`) as you hear it, **or the letter the word spells it with**: *profitable* is [[profitable|PRAF/+U/+TU/+-BL]] and [[profitable|PRAF/+O/+TO/+-BL]].
**A weak last syllable that fits on the stroke before it can fold onto it**: [[sensible|SEPB/+SU/+-BL]] or [[sensible|SEPB/+SUBL]].

blocks.x: Split anywhere you hear a break

Several splits are valid; all are in the dictionary. *lem-on* is [[lemon|HREPL/+UPB]] and *le-mon* is [[lemon|HRE/+PHUPB]]. *compromise* can be *com-pro-mise*, [[compromise|KOPL/+PR/+PHAOEUZ]] (*comp-ro-mise*) or [[compromise|KOPL/+PROPL/+AOEUZ]] (*compro-mise*). Any consonant run that can start a syllable may go to the next stroke or stay.

A stroke is any run of sounds with at most one vowel, so three to six strokes all work: *complete* is [[complete|KU/+PH/+HRAOET]], [[complete|K/+UPL/+PHRAOET]], [[complete|KU/+-PL/+-P/+HRAOET]]. The cheapest few of each length are in the dictionary. Prefer fewer strokes.
A word with no memorised outline: say it, strike its syllables. Every dictionary word of two or more syllables is reachable by at least one of these splits.

opts: the join key `+` on strokes 2 and 3
blocks.why: It is [[PHU/+SHE/+TAOE]]. Without the `+`, each stroke would be a separate word.
